season.evidence: Logged ascents of the peak are Jul 3, Aug 2, Sep 5 (plus 2 in April, 1 in November); a rock ridge above a river ford that runs cold and high in July, so Aug-Sep is easier. No stored season; Jul-Sep matches the standard line.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Logged as West notch from Hardscrabble (Aug 2015); climbs the west notch with an east-face scramble down, not the north ridge; starts at the horse camp, not our gate pin.
July 2023 ascent by the northwest slopes from Hardscrabble; no north-ridge climbing, no logged route.
Sept 2023 west couloir (three class 4 steps) then NE face descent; a different line, and not harvested as a track.

facts.text: In early September the Middle Fork ford, found about a mile upstream where a wash meets the river near 3,100 ft, was a careful rock-hop on slippery stones rather than a deep wade; the far bank opens with head-high huckleberry before easing into open forest.

notes: The only route here, North Ridge (1971, low class 5), has no matching recording: every harvested ascent used the west notch/couloir or northwest slopes from Hardscrabble. Our summit pin is 119 m from the surveyed summit, but the peak has two near-equal summits 100+ m apart (northwest and southeast; a 2023 report puts the register on the southeast) and the tracks pass within ~3 m of our pin, so no summit move is proposed. The Trailhead pin is the Dingford Creek gate (~8 km before the horse camp); recordings start at Hardscrabble, already a Campsite pin; no trailhead move is warranted. A separate standard route (west notch/couloir, class 4) is absent from the catalog and has three summited tracks.
